discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: In 2013 IceCube reported a flux of high-energy neutrinos of extraterrestrial origin, opening a new window on the universe. Neutrinos are ideal messengers: they are not deflected by magnetic fields and they escape dense environments that light cannot. Later work identified individual sources, the blazar TXS 0506+056 in 2017 and the active galaxy NGC 1068 in 2022, and in 2023 IceCube imaged the Milky Way in neutrinos. Francis Halzen conceived the idea of turning a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a particle detector and pursued it for decades, from AMANDA to IceCube. A simple idea was extremely hard to realise technically, and he made it happen through a patient international effort. The citation is narrow: the first detection of cosmic high-energy neutrinos, which founded neutrino astronomy at these energies. It was not an improvement on existing techniques. It was a new kind of observation of nature.
